gap_rulings.GAP-372: ACCEPTABLE documented limit: credentials are stripped through all 12 URL-legal connectors and queries are cut (explicit4.json); only a local path / user-directory name glued after a URL is stored. Path/origin only.
gap_rulings.GAP-373: Leaks the user name and the password PREFIX. Raw space / raw slash: acceptable as documented (not a valid userinfo). %2F / %252F (the correct encoding of a / in a password): leak created by decoding before stripping; documented in GAP-373, so not counted as undocumented, but minor understates it; fix with A4-F2.

root_cause_hypothesis: The rule is a pipeline of destructive passes whose order lets one pass erase the evidence the next relies on: decode-before-parse (A4-F2, GAP-373 %2F) and userinfo-strip-before-cut (A4-F1/F1b; fix-3 D2). Each cycle reordered or widened a pass to close the last shape; every generator places one construct per string, so pass interactions are never exercised. Spec right, implementation wrong, tests share the blind spot.
revised_plan: Structured fields: parse the RAW string with WHATWG URL first, emit origin + pathname (never userinfo), then decode / apply the text rule to that output; on a parse failure with an @ after // before the next /, emit [redacted].
Free text: when the span the userinfo strip would remove contains a (decoded) ? # ; = or &, treat it as a cut at the span start instead of deleting those characters.

Pairwise-interaction property test (cut char x @ x = x encoded forms, both orders, every surface) plus a differential oracle: nothing that follows a cut character in the decoded input may appear in the output.
